interest: Although brief, this index file illustrates the State Department's decimal filing system and the administrative mechanism for tracking bilateral tax reciprocity at both the national and sub-national levels during the interwar period. It specifically highlights how state-level legislation—here, New York State laws concerning taxes on decedents' estates—interacted with Japanese inheritance law, requiring diplomatic inquiry and recording by Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Tokyo. It also provides a useful archival cross-reference directing researchers to general file 800.5124/10 for the substantive correspondence.
overview: This file consists of a single Department of State List of Papers sheet (Form DS-46) filed under decimal number 894.5124, designated for Japanese inheritance tax law and financial affairs. The sheet indexes a single document: Despatch No. 674 dated February 15, 1934, from U.S. Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Japan. The entry notes reciprocity with Japan pursuant to the provisions of New York State laws regarding taxes on decedents' estates, and cross-references the substantive documentation to the general international decimal file 800.5124/10.
